pages.text: $(thing)Sun curing$() requires daytime, sky light of at least $(item)14$() above the rack, no direct rain, and an open structure with at least $(item)2 horizontal sides$() next to the rack made of air.

With direct sky access, sun curing takes $(item)48,000 ticks$(), about $(item)2 Minecraft days$(). A glass or stained-glass block/pane immediately above the rack may replace direct sky access, but that covered-glass method takes $(item)54,000 ticks$() (2.25 days).
pages.title: Direct vs. Glass Sun

pages.text: When $(thing)Create$() is installed, plain Encased Fan airflow accelerates an otherwise-valid Sun Cure without changing its identity. A wooden rack needs qualifying airflow to reach one rack probe. An $(item)Industrial Drying Rack$() still requires matching plain airflow at both levels from two distinct fans. Direct-sky and glass-sheltered Sun Curing can both be assisted.
pages.title: Fan-Assisted Sun Cure
Hanging / Pergola Sun
pages.text: Hanging bunches use a different sun check because their attachment block always blocks the sky above them. They Sun Cure when an adjacent horizontal air column can see strong daytime sky light. Alternating $(item)beam / gap / beam / gap$() rows therefore work as a pergola; a continuous solid roof with no side skylight becomes Air Curing.

At night, with weak skylight, or when the structure becomes too enclosed, sun curing pauses or another valid method takes over. Rain exposure is especially dangerous because it damages quality and can eventually spoil the batch.
